messages:
Ana (People Ops): Heads-up — Sam mentioned on onboarding that he's moving his legal work base to the UK starting May 1. Need to sync payroll cutover, pension auto-enrolment, and how the home-office allowance gets handled in GBP.
Sam Patel: Yep that's right — May 1 is the target. I need to keep benefits active and would like my monthly WFH allowance to continue (currently USD 150/mo).
Jess Ortiz: Quick Q — do we treat the WFH allowance as taxable income in the UK? I remember differences vs US.
Emma (Legal): UK: generally allowances paid by employer are taxable and count toward gross pay unless structured as reimbursed expenses with receipts. Also auto-enrolment pension rules trigger based on PAYE earnings. We'll need to check thresholds.
Liam - Payroll: Ok. Practical next steps: 1) final USD payroll run date (last US payment) 2) UK payroll onboarding for Sam (NI, tax code, pension provider setup) 3) bank details (GBP preferred) 4) stop/start dates for benefits. When is Sam's last workday tied to US payroll?
Sam Patel: Last US-paid period would be the pay period ending Apr 24. I can confirm bank details this week. Prefer getting paid in GBP via UK bank if possible.
Ana (People Ops): Noted. Jess & Liam — can Payroll do a split-month handling so Sam doesn't get double contributions? We need to avoid duplicate pension enrollments and ensure HMRC/tax code is correct.
Liam - Payroll: We can do a final gross-up in USD run and then start UK PAYE from May 1. Pension: we'll hold off auto-enrol until we confirm pensionable earnings in the UK payroll system. Need Sam's NI number and UK bank account.
Jess Ortiz: For the WFH allowance, should we convert to GBP and keep the same nominal value or peg to purchasing power? Also payroll tax treatment will change the net amount Sam receives.
Emma (Legal): Recommend we convert to a flat GBP amount equivalent to median exchange rate over last 3 months to avoid big swings, and mark it as taxable pay in the UK payroll. If Sam prefers reimbursement model (submit receipts for a one-off desk chair, etc.), that can be non-taxable if bona fide expense.
Ana (People Ops): Action items: - Sam to provide NI and UK bank by EOD Thu - Liam to confirm final USD run date and set UK onboarding date May 1 - Jess to calculate GBP equivalent for WFH allowance and give options for taxable vs reimbursement - Emma to confirm pension provider and auto-enrol timing.
Sam Patel: Will send NI and bank by tomorrow. Also, I have an open equipment reimbursement claim (desk monitor) — will that interfere with cutover?
Liam - Payroll: Equipment reimbursements that were approved on the US payroll can be paid before cutover. If submitted after May 1, process via UK expense flow. Please cc payroll@redwood when you send paperwork.
HRBot: Reminder: update your Home Base in Workday at least 10 business days before move to ensure correct benefits enrollment windows.
Jess Ortiz: One more: PTO bank differences. UK holiday ladder and accrual can differ vs US policies. Ana — we'll need to prorate Sam's annual allowance for 2026 and confirm carryover rules.
Ana (People Ops): Agreed. I'll draft a short email to Sam with the timeline and who does what. Will also include link to the cross-border relocation FAQ.
Emma (Legal): Also flag potential tax-nexus questions if Sam keeps occasional US client work or travels >183 days. We'll need to track days in US.
Sam Patel: I'll keep a travel log and ping you if anything changes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Ana (People Ops): Thanks — I'll follow up with the timeline in a DM and add tasks to the relocation checklist.
notes: This thread is an operational coordination discussion about changing legal work base to the UK, payroll cutover, pension auto-enrolment, home-office allowance conversion, equipment reimbursements, and PTO/proration. Contains action items and owner assignments.
